--- round 1, driver 1:
Leg 2 ended DNF after 9 rail touches, mostly the trailer's rear-right corner. Tiny hitch-target steering let the rear drift onto the right rail while reversing straight, and each pin set off gear-change cycling that burned touches. Keep the trailer rear centred between the rails from the start and correct drift while it is small. Reverse slowly. Avoid heavy steer on forward pulls, which put the front-left corner on the left rail. After a pin, a short straight forward pull cleared the rear corner best. Avoid repeated gear cycling. Expect the rail side to change along the sbend.
--- round 1, driver 2:
DNF: too many rail touches, nearly all on the trailer's rear-right corner against the right rail. Reversing with small hitch angles, the rear drifted right and corrections came too late; each pin cost a penalty and a forward clear. Hard full-lock swings left threw the trailer far left and clipped the left rail with the front-left corner. Priorities: centre the trailer rear early, keep it biased left of the right rail, reverse slowly, and correct offset before the hitch builds. Avoid repeated short forward pulls that rack up gear changes; one clean clear, then gentle steering.

Early reverse was fine, but the rear drifted right and each fix became a forward-and-reverse cycle costing a penalty and another touch. Prioritise keeping the rear centred, correcting gently and early as it drifts toward a rail, and keeping the hitch small. Avoid repeated forward pulls: they cost gear changes and did not free the corner. Once pinned, do not thrash with big steering swings. Tip: this long trailer reacts slowly, so small early steering beats large late corrections.
